name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Rupiah near record lows after Bank Indonesia raised rates to 6% on 18 Nov; no EM default or IMF rescue found
state: Bank Indonesia unexpectedly raised its benchmark rate by 0.25 points to 6% on 18 Nov after a record low near 18,290 per dollar earlier that week; the rupiah closed at 18,255 on 19 Nov and hovered near 18,270 on 20 Nov, about 9% weaker in 2026 (Bisnis Indonesia; Trading Economics). Pressure comes from a strong dollar, Fed rate-rise bets and fund outflows, while Q3 current account data showed the deficit narrowing to $2.0bn. The currency has not fallen 10% in a month, and no major emerging economy in default or seeking emergency IMF support was found as of 21 Nov.
for_you: Emerging economies with dollar debts and importers paying in dollars are most exposed while US rates rise; further Fed rises tend to add pressure on weaker currencies.
rubric_hit: Normal: rupiah down ~9% in 2026, not >10% in a month; no EM default, capital controls or IMF emergency support

sources.title: Trading Economics — Rupiah recovers but heads for weekly losses
Bisnis Indonesia — Rupiah ditutup melemah ke Rp18.255 per dolar AS (19/11)

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
